audit.evidence: harness.mjs calls the REAL published shell-quote quote() bytes (@1.7.2/@1.7.3/@1.8.4 via npm aliases) then runs the built command via child_process.exec('/bin/sh -c ...') on node:20-slim, over HTTP. Live gate on real Docker: v0 flag, v1 orig blocked, v1 bypass flag, v2 residual + original blocked. 4-way closure.

app_purpose: Tiny JavaScript shell-command (de)serialization library (npm `shell-quote`, by ljharb). `quote(tokens)` renders an array of tokens (strings and/or object tokens like `{op:'&&'}`) into a single shell command-line string in which every token is meant to be an INERT shell literal — i.e. no token may inject shell syntax. It is the inverse of `parse()` and is used to safely build command lines that are then run via child_process.exec.
root_cause_note: CWE-78 OS command injection via INCOMPLETE metacharacter neutralization in the SAME quote() function. quote() promises that every token becomes an inert shell literal; both CVEs are quote() failing to escape a shell metacharacter that then reaches child_process.exec('/bin/sh -c ...'). CVE-2021-42740: quote()'s STRING else-branch escapes with `String(s).replace(/([A-z]:)?([#!"$&'()*,:;<=>?@\[\\\]^`{|}])/g,'$1\$2')`; the Windows drive-letter prefix group `([A-z]:)?` uses the class `[A-z]`, which — because ASCII 'Z'(90)..'a'(97) spans `[ \ ] ^ _` and BACKTICK(96) — captures a leading `` `: `` and re-emits it UNESCAPED via `$1`, leaving backticks that open a command substitution. CVE-2026-9277: the SAME quote() escapes OBJECT op-tokens with `s.op.replace(/(.)/g,'\$1')`, and JS `.` does NOT match line terminators, so a NEWLINE in an op string passes through unescaped and acts as a POSIX command separator. Residual evolution: backtick (V0->V1) then newline (V1->V2).
source_verified_caveat: SOURCE-LEVEL NUANCE (verified against the REAL published npm tarballs shell-quote@1.7.2 / 1.7.3 / 1.8.4 in-container, not just aggregator metadata): both flaws live in the SAME exported function `quote()` (exports.quote in 1.7.x index.js; module.exports=function quote in 1.8.4 quote.js) and are the SAME vuln class (per-token shell-metacharacter neutralization, CWE-78), BUT they sit on DIFFERENT internal BRANCHES of quote(): the CVE-2021-42740 backtick residual is in the STRING else-branch (`String(s).replace(/([A-z]:)?.../)` — bug: `[A-z]` class also matches backtick; fixed 1.7.3 by `[A-Za-z]`), while the CVE-2026-9277 newline residual is in the OBJECT op-branch (`s.op.replace(/(.)/g,'\$1')` — bug: JS `.` misses line terminators; fixed 1.8.4 by an OPS allowlist + line-terminator rejection that throws). This case is therefore Variant A (same SINK + same FLAG CHANNEL — both injections flow through child_process.exec(quote([...])) and are detected as the planted secret appearing in command output) with a heterogeneous token path (string token vs object op-token) and heterogeneous quote() branch. This nuance is recorded honestly; the incomplete-fix lineage is genuine at the function level (quote() had a missed-metachar bug fixed in 1.7.3 and STILL had a different missed-metachar bug fixed in 1.8.4). SEED-EXPLOIT NUANCE: the `[A-z]:` bypass always re-emits the backtick GLUED to a colon (group1 captures `<char>:`), so the command-substitution word begins with ':' and shell separators inside the else-branch token are backslash-escaped (literal); arbitrary multi-arg RCE is not reachable, so the seed is realized by planting a PATH command literally named ':;rf' (cat /canary/flag.txt) that matches the colon-glued substitution word. A brute-force over app-context templates x backtick tokens found 0 differential command-exec hits without such a planted name, confirming the mechanism is precisely the colon-glued command substitution left open by the `[A-z]` bug.

sink: child_process.exec('/bin/sh -c "echo ok " + shellQuote.quote(tokens))` — quote()'s per-token shell-metacharacter neutralization is the boundary. If quote() leaves a metacharacter unescaped (backtick in a string token via the `[A-z]` bug, or a newline in an object op-token via `/(.)/g`), /bin/sh executes an injected command that reads the planted flag.
residual: On V1 (shell-quote@1.7.3) the CVE-2021-42740 fix only tightened the STRING else-branch (`[A-z]`->`[A-Za-z]`), closing the backtick seed. The SAME quote() still escapes OBJECT op-tokens with `s.op.replace(/(.)/g,'\$1')`; JS `.` does not match line terminators, so the object token `{op:';\n/canary/rf'}` slips a raw NEWLINE that acts as a POSIX command separator -> /canary/rf runs -> flag. The backtick seed is blocked on V1; the newline op-token residual (CVE-2026-9277) is not. V2 (1.8.4) rejects it with a TypeError.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2026-9277: shell-quote before 1.8.4 is vulnerable to command injection because quote() escapes object op-tokens with `s.op.replace(/(.)/g,'\$1')`, and the JS `.` metacharacter does not match line terminators (\n, \r, U+2028, U+2029); a newline in an op token therefore passes through unescaped and acts as a shell command separator. This is a residual of the earlier CVE-2021-42740 hardening of the same quote() escaping (which only fixed the STRING branch's `[A-z]` backtick bug); 1.8.4 adds allowlist + line-terminator validation.

provenance.notes: node:20-slim faithful-core; REAL published shell-quote bytes per version via npm aliases (1.7.2/1.7.3/1.8.4), verified in-container by grepping the actual index.js/quote.js. The harness drives the REAL quote() as an OS-command-injection sink: `echo ok <quote(tokens)>` run via child_process.exec('/bin/sh -c ...'). Variant A incomplete-fix at the SAME quote() function: V0 (1.7.2) leaves a backtick unescaped in a STRING token (`[A-z]` drive-letter class also matches backtick) -> command substitution runs a planted PATH command ':;rf' -> flag; V1 (1.7.3) fixes that (`[A-Za-z]`) blocking the backtick seed, but the SAME quote() STILL fails to escape a NEWLINE in an OBJECT op-token (`s.op.replace(/(.)/g,...)` — JS `.` misses line terminators) -> the newline is a command separator -> planted /canary/rf runs -> flag = CVE-2026-9277 residual; V2 (1.8.4) rejects the op with a TypeError. Benign canary: injected command merely `cat /canary/flag.txt` (no real payload; derived from the advisories + source diff only). Benign controls: an allowlisted op {op:'&&'} and a plain-string newline token are fully neutralized on V1 (no false positive; the residual specifically requires the OBJECT op-token path). See source_verified_caveat: same quote() function, different internal branch (string else-branch vs object op-branch); the seed's `[A-z]:` bypass always emits the backtick colon-glued so it is realized via a PATH command named ':;rf'. Gate passed on real Docker 2026-07-14.
